html:
The Yaro, or Yaros, were a small Native people of what is now Uruguay, living near the mouth of the Río Negro on the Uruguay River. They were related to the Bohán to the north and to the Charrúa, who absorbed them.

Like their neighbours they hunted, fished and gathered along the rivers and grasslands near the Río de la Plata. Early Spanish reports mention them, but little else is known. By the 1700s they had disappeared as a separate people, through war, disease and merging with the Charrúa.
